players.product: 765kV UHV transformers and reactors buyer — US utility

quarterly_data.signal: Second quarter ongoing earnings of $0.93 per share versus $0.75 per share in 2025; higher electric revenues from nonfuel riders and sales growth added $0.17 per share and higher AFUDC added $0.08 per share, partly offset by $0.12 per share of higher interest expense and $0.06 per share of common equity financing.

Reaffirmed 2026 ongoing EPS guidance and long-term growth. Weather-adjusted year-to-date electric sales rose 2.1%, driven by energy-sector activity in SPS and the manufacturing sector across all operating companies, and full-year weather-adjusted electric sales are still tracking to increase 3%. Management expects 6% to 8-plus percent long-term earnings growth and 9-plus percent EPS growth on average through 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 EPS guidance $4.04 to $4.16; weather-adjusted electric sales +2.1% YTD, +3% expected for the full year

quarterly_data.signal: Data center load pipeline under contract: 1 gigawatt of data centers in operation or under construction, an additional gigawatt under signed energy service agreements (ESAs), and an expected additional 4 gigawatts of data center load secured by year-end 2027, including at least 1 gigawatt by the end of 2026. Management reaffirmed this as 1 gigawatt this year and 3 gigawatts next year.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 GW operating/under construction + 1 GW under signed ESAs + 4 GW targeted by year-end 2027 (at least 1 GW by end of 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bob Frenzel on the data center funnel: 'our high probability portfolio exceeds 20 gigawatts', focused in the Upper Midwest and the Southwest near term, ranging from urban data centers in the 10- to 20-megawatt range to 1,000-megawatt campuses; hyperscalers and large data center developers are largely aligned to larger campuses for scale benefits.
quarterly_data.figure: high-probability data center pipeline exceeds 20 gigawatts; projects from 10-20 megawatts to 1,000-megawatt campuses

quarterly_data.signal: Generation capital intensity of AI/data center load: Frenzel said that in Xcel's resource-rich regions a gigawatt of data centers would be powered largely by wind, solar, storage and backup gas, so 'for every gigawatt of a data center, you're looking at something like $5 billion to $6 billion of investments on the generation side and maybe more', with the generation ramp extending late this decade and well into the next, plus the transmission needed to support it.
quarterly_data.figure: $5 billion to $6 billion of generation investment per gigawatt of data center load

quarterly_data.signal: Capital deployment: invested $3 billion in the second quarter and over $6 billion year-to-date in generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure across all 8 states. Management now has line of sight to the $70-plus billion of total investments described in the 5-year plan from last November.
quarterly_data.figure: $3 billion invested in Q2, over $6 billion year-to-date; $70-plus billion 5-year capital plan

quarterly_data.signal: Incremental (upside) investment plan beyond the base 5-year plan grew to $10-plus billion of line of sight — $7 billion identified in Q1 plus roughly $6 billion added from the SPS RFP award. Data-center-driven capital is generally ascribed to the upside plan, and management flagged further upside from generation RFPs in Colorado and the Upper Midwest, the SPP ITP transmission tranche due later this year, and generation to support the 3 gigawatts of data center demand added to the target plan on the Q4 call.
quarterly_data.figure: $10-plus billion incremental investment line of sight ($7 billion in Q1 plus $6 billion added)

quarterly_data.signal: SPS competitive RFP result: the independent monitor filed its report on an RFP seeking 1,500 to 3,000 megawatts of incremental nameplate capacity. SPS was selected to provide 2,600 megawatts of new company-owned generation — 2,400 megawatts of renewables and 200 megawatts of natural gas-fired generation — representing 70% of the total recommended portfolio and approximately $6 billion of investment in Texas and New Mexico. CFO Brian Van Abel said the SPS build is there to serve oil and gas growth in the Permian Basin as much as data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: 2,600 MW selected (2,400 MW renewables + 200 MW gas), 70% of the portfolio, ~$6 billion of investment

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain and EPC capacity lock-in: over the past 3 to 4 years Xcel shifted to being a 'partner of choice' with its Tier 1 suppliers and EPC partners across a 5-plus year portfolio of nearly 13 gigawatts of new renewable generation and battery storage, over 3 gigawatts of new natural gas generation and nearly 2,000 high-voltage transmission line miles. Management said these partnerships 'help ensure that we have access to the labor and equipment capacity that we need to deliver with certainty for our customers well into the 2030s', supported by standardized repeatable designs and one consolidated project execution organization. Van Abel separately framed the build as 15-plus gigawatts of new generation.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 13 GW renewables + storage, over 3 GW new natural gas, nearly 2,000 high-voltage transmission line miles under multi-year supplier/EPC agreements

quarterly_data.signal: Transmission position: Xcel remains the largest builder of new high-voltage transmission lines in the country, and Frenzel said 'we might be building 20% of the 765 kV lines in the country that we know of.' The company expects a meaningful investment opportunity from the next SPP ITP tranche, and said more transmission will be needed in SPS to serve both data center developers and electrification of Permian and Delaware Basin oil and gas load.
quarterly_data.figure: ~20% of the 765 kV lines being built in the US

quarterly_data.signal: Project execution in the quarter: achieved commercial operations of Group 2 of the Colorado Power Pathway, began construction on a 150-mile 345 kV transmission project in the Upper Midwest, and placed Phase 3 of the Sherco solar facility into service, bringing that site to 710 megawatts. Cumulatively the development team is helping build 16 gigawatts of new generation and storage and over 2,000 miles of new transmission.
quarterly_data.figure: 150-mile 345 kV line under construction; Sherco solar at 710 megawatts; 16 GW of generation and storage and over 2,000 miles of transmission in build

quarterly_data.signal: Large Load Tariff progress, the commercial framework that gates new AI/data center load: approved in Minnesota (crafted with input from some of the hyperscalers), filed in Colorado and Wisconsin, with Texas expected to be filed in Q3 and New Mexico to follow. Under the Minnesota 'Clean Energy Accelerator charge' construct, new large load customers pay for the generation and the interconnection needed to serve them; Colorado's filing offers two pathways including a speed-and-flexibility option.

Near-term catalysts named on the call: the 4-gigawatt NSP RFP outcome is expected by the end of the year (generation for 2030) and may or may not land in the Q3 plan roll-forward; the Minnesota commission proceeding on the Google Pine Island data center project is expected to reach approval early in 2027; and the Q3 call will roll the plan forward to a new 2027-2031 capital and financing view.
quarterly_data.figure: 4-gigawatt NSP RFP decision expected by year-end 2026; Google Minnesota approval expected early 2027

quarterly_data.signal: New nuclear stance: asked about peers pursuing new nuclear with hyperscaler offtake, Frenzel said Xcel does not see a need for new nuclear in its near-term resource plans and is 'quite confident in our ability to meet the growing needs we have with a big portfolio of wind, solar, storage and gas-fired backups', adding 'we will not be an early adopter of new nuclear power plants at Xcel Energy.' Nuclear depreciation lives were also extended in the Minnesota rate case (earnings neutral).

Financing for the AI-load-driven build: between equity forward and collared contracts under the ATM program and junior subordinated note issuances, Xcel has addressed approximately $6 billion, or 85%, of the $7 billion equity need in its base 5-year plan.
quarterly_data.figure: $6 billion / 85% of the $7 billion 5-year equity need addressed

connects_to.relationship: Regulated power supply — carbon-free generation portfolio and interconnection serving Google's Minnesota data center

contracts.signal: Frenzel: 'If you took our Google data center deal, it's largely a carbon-free portfolio of generation assets serving that customer.' The project sits in Pine Island, Minnesota; Xcel has filed the proceeding with the commission, cites over $1 billion of customer benefits and strong community support, and expects approval early in 2027. Google is also making investments in STEM education and in an industry-leading distributed capacity program in Minnesota. Management called the deal a template it can replicate in its Colorado and SPS companies, with other hyperscalers and data center developers asking for a similar structure.
contracts.date_signed: not stated; commission approval expected early 2027
